islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world

# ghost to circle).

channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

  set injection = max(thing, source) / (0.879 + 0.7099 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 0.8979
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.6751 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1.557 - leak))

observations.text:
The agent spends its whole life inside one small walled pocket (a 4x12 box, start and death in the same spot), sweeping back and forth along it and never leaving, so it never even reaches the food lying a short walk away in the neighbouring rooms.
It does press and break things (3 doors, 5 breaks), but after each press it drifts back into the pocket instead of walking through, so the openings it makes do not turn into a route out.
The failure is that inside a sealed pocket every boundary cell is known solid, so there are no frontier marks (unknown cells touching known-free ones) and the value field has nothing to point at except leak through walls, which is weak and spread evenly around the whole box.
A fix: give solid cells that have unknown space behind them (a wall with darkness on its far side, especially one whose leak was taught high by a door opening) a source of their own when no frontier exists, so the wave leads the agent into one specific wall and through it, and keep that target (a lingering source) until it is passed.

Early in life the agent ranges widely and eats steadily (most meals lie along the long cyan path), but in the late part it gets stuck in one spot at the lower left, looping in tight circles inside a 13x13 box for its last stretch with no meals there.
Many of the remaining food dots sit inside small walled rooms (the outlined squares), and the agent opened 0 doors while making 100 idle presses, so it is being called by food it can smell or see behind walls and keeps pressing stone instead of finding the room's door.
The loops look like the wave leaking through the nearest wall toward the smelled food: the agent is led into the same stone, presses, slides off, circles back, and repeats.
A fix: remember the wall cells it has pressed without result (solid cells next to `here` that stay solid) and stop letting the wave leak through those cells for a long while, so the path through the wall moves to other cells of the room's boundary until it reaches the door, or the agent gives up and leaves.

The agent is born in the same small two-corridor pocket as before and again spends its whole life there: it walks more than the earlier champion (615 cells of distance vs 284) but only ever over the same ~58 cells, sweeping from end to end until it starves at the far end of the upper corridor.
The pocket's only ways out are the brown door/rubble tiles at its ends and below it, and it opened just one door and broke five things while making 21 idle presses, so most of its pressing lands on rock rather than on those tiles.
Food is a few cells away in the neighbouring rooms, but behind solid walls the wave sees only an even leak through every wall cell, so nothing makes a door tile stand out from the rock around it, and once a press fails the agent swings back to the other end.
One mechanism: make the wave leak through a wall cell in proportion to how unlike the surrounding rock it is (the taught per-hue `leak` contrasted against its neighbours' leak, e.g. leak minus the mean leak of the wall cells around it), so door and rubble tiles become the bright exits of a sealed pocket and the agent presses them rather than the rock.

Same world, same trap: the agent is born in the small two-corridor pocket and spends its whole life sweeping it (65 cells visited, a 4x12 box for its last 500 ticks) until it starves at the east end, with food a few cells away in the neighbouring rooms.
It is not passive: it opened 5 doors and broke 5 things, but made 106 idle presses, and after each opening it swings back into the pocket instead of stepping through, so the openings never become a way out.
The pull that brings it back is the pocket itself: all values are local and short-lived, and the footprint trail fades within a few thoughts, so each time it turns round the far end of the pocket looks fresh again.
One mechanism: a slow HABITUATION field that accumulates wherever the agent spends time (much slower to fade than the trail) and dims the value there, so after a few hundred ticks in one small area everything familiar is dark and the only bright cells left are beyond the doors it has opened.

The new best law fails world 16 exactly like its predecessors: born in the two-corridor pocket, it sweeps the same ~63 cells for its whole life and starves at the east end, never reaching the food in the rooms around it.
What changed is the pressing: 182 idle presses and 0 doors or breaks (earlier laws opened 1-5 doors here), so the door contrast now concentrates its pushes on a few rock cells instead of spreading them, and none of those cells is one of the brown door/rubble tiles at the pocket's ends and below it.
The contrast can only light a door once the door's hue has been pressed and taught; a door never pressed keeps the innate leak and does not stand out from untaught rock, while repeatedly pressed rock is the cell the wave keeps returning to.
One mechanism: make a wall cell's pull through the wave decay with the number of presses it has already received without giving (a per-cell, not per-hue, refusal count that dims its leak), so after a few failed pushes on one rock cell the next-best wall cell becomes the target and every boundary cell of a pocket, the doors included, eventually gets tried.

turns.hypothesis: Every frontier mark is worth the same 0.12 today, so a one-cell unknown pocket beside a wall pulls as hard as the edge of a large unexplored region. Weighting each frontier mark by the smoothed amount of unknown around it (information gain) sends the agent toward big unseen areas where new food is likely, while smell and seen morsels keep their value and the confinement suppression is kept.

A reactive wave lets the agent step back onto the cell it just left whenever two targets are nearly equal, which wastes ticks in back-and-forth limit cycles. A fading footprint channel (trail = max(here, decay*trail), scrolling with the map) dims what the agent READS on its own recent path while the plan wave itself stays untouched, so it commits forward and sweeps instead of dithering, but can still return when the way back is clearly better.

One discount serves two different promises: food (certain, worth a detour only when near) and the frontier (uncertain, but only informative if the agent commits to a long walk). Splitting the wave into an exploitation wave with a steep discount and an exploration wave with a shallow discount, read as their max, lets far frontiers keep a coherent long-range pull while nearby food still wins when close.

When frontiers on several sides look alike, the agent's target can switch from thought to thought and it sweeps nothing completely. A frozen random preference per place (seeded once, inherited by cells scrolling in, smoothed into regions, and carried with the map) breaks such ties the same way every thought, so the agent commits to one side of the unknown and explores it through; the frontier/food split is also computed inline now, removing a one-pass lag that injected a stale full-strength peak.

Exploration is driven only by frontier marks, which exist only where unknown ground touches known-free ground; once the agent has seen every wall of a room, cave or pocket, the value field has nothing to aim at and it sweeps the box until it starves (the observer's world-16 life). A BREACH source on every reachable wall cell with darkness behind it, weighted by the darkness and passed through the wall's taught leak, is weak enough that any food or frontier beats it in the max, but when nothing else calls it leads the agent into the most promising wall, where pressing opens doors and chips rubble; stone that never gives is taught a low leak and drops out, so the agent tries walls in turn. Food in this world grows on fixed spots that regrow on a timer, yet every law so far forgets a spot as soon as its sighting fades, so the agent re-finds food only by luck. A long LARDER memory of where good morsels were seen, multiplied by a RIPENESS clock that is reset whenever the agent stands on or beside the place and climbs slowly back, injects a source that calls the agent back to a patch about when it should have regrown: a trapline over the remembered map, on top of the darkness-weighted frontier and the footprint trail.

My theory says extra competing pulls distract; modulating the frontier helps (darkness weighting, footprint trail). The smell is painted at a single point along a bearing that flips around walls, so following it directly is fragile, but it says roughly where food is. A broad slowly fading AROMA halo around recent smell points multiplies frontier marks inside it, so exploration is biased toward unknown ground in the smelled direction (finding the actual path around the wall) instead of toward any dark region, with no new competing source.

Every law so far is a max-wave, which follows the single best target and ignores how much is there: one frontier cell and a whole dark region, one berry and a patch of five pull alike once discounted. Replacing the race with a RELAXATION (each free cell becomes the mean of its neighbours, sources fixed, zero at the outer ring and in walls) gives a harmonic potential with no local maxima away from sources, where many sources in one direction add up, so the agent heads for where most food and most unknown lie and cannot be trapped between two equal targets.

Exploration so far is local and isotropic: the darkness-weighted frontier wave keeps the agent re-sweeping the same neighbourhood, while food regrows on fixed spots spread over the whole world. A slowly turning world-fixed COMPASS (a life clock carried by the map, and each cell's projection on a heading that rotates once every few thousand ticks) multiplies frontier marks that lie ahead, so the agent makes long straight excursions into new land and comes round to every side over a life, while food and smell are untouched and still win when present.

The map forgets a wall at the same rate as everything else, so a wall seen a few hundred ticks ago becomes half transparent to the wave and then "unknown" again: the agent is led through stale walls into presses that do nothing and back to re-inspect stone as if it were frontier. A MASONRY memory keeps walls nearly permanent (cleared only where the cell is seen free, so opened doors and chipped rubble disappear), and confinement, darkness, frontier and the wave's passability all read it, while free ground and food are still forgotten so regrowth gets revisited.

The smell is repainted from scratch every thought at a waypoint whose bearing flips between the two ways round a wall, so food-directed walks can dither even with the footprint trail; the plain ghost helped the bare wave by +4 meals but was never tried on top of darkness-weighted exploration. Here only FOOD evidence (smell and seen morsels) lingers in its own NOSE channel, erased when the agent reaches the spot or when it is marked bad, while frontier marks stay instantaneous, so a food target once chosen is held through the flip but exploration still follows the live map.

Confinement (a count of solid neighbours) cannot tell a dead-end nook, where a source is a trap, from a doorway or corridor mouth, where the frontier opens onto a whole new room; it suppresses both. Reading the map's GEOMETRY with shifted walls separates them: a dead end (three or four sides walled) suppresses sources, a passage (walled on one opposite pair, open on the other) multiplies frontier marks at and beside it, so the agent leaves rooms through their doors instead of combing their corners.

The observer saw the agent end its life looping in one spot with 100 idle presses and 0 doors, called by food inside walled rooms: the wave leaks through the nearest wall cell, so it is led into the same stone again and again. A STONE memory builds up on wall cells the body keeps leaning on that stay solid (and clears where a cell turns out free), and the wave's leak through a wall is scaled by (1 - stone), so a pressed-and-failed cell stops carrying the wave, the route "through" slides along the room's boundary to the door, or the call fades and the agent leaves to forage elsewhere.

The persistent max-wave never forgets fast enough: when a morsel is eaten or a smell waypoint moves, its old peak leaves a flat plateau that decays only as fast as it spreads, so for several thoughts every neighbour ties and the gradients of the real current sources are hidden under it (the agent walks blind straight ahead after each meal). A FRESH plan wiped on the first pass of every thought (a life clock gives the phase) and rebuilt from what is sensed now is added to a scaled-down persistent wave that keeps the long view, so the near decision always follows live evidence while the far guidance survives.

The agent is slow (world 2: 0.22 cells per tick) because the brightest neighbour changes direction often and every turn costs thrust; and wiping the persistent wave (#16, 12.8) showed that holding a course is worth a lot. A MOMENTUM read-out marks the neighbour of the agent that lies straight ahead (opposite the freshest footprint, found with shifted trail and here fields) and boosts it a little, so the agent keeps its heading unless the plan clearly prefers a turn, walking straighter and faster between targets; the plan wave itself is unchanged.

The wave prices every non-solid cell the same, so a plan to a smell waypoint or a far frontier runs straight through unknown ground as if it were open floor, and the agent is led into walls and dead ends it could not see. Making the step cost depend on KNOWLEDGE (an extra discount for each unknown cell crossed, none on known-free floor) makes the plan prefer routes over ground it has seen, and it weighs a target behind unexplored terrain as the gamble it is, without adding any new source or changing the read-out.

In sealed pockets and walled rooms (the observer's world 16 and world 2: many presses, few doors) the wave leaks through every wall cell alike, so the nearest rock is pressed as often as the door. The harness already teaches the leak per hue (a door that opens raises it, rock that does nothing lowers it); a DOORNESS contrast amplifies a wall cell's leak by how much it exceeds the mean leak of the solid cells around it, so a door or rubble tile in a rock wall becomes the one bright exit, while the knowledge-priced wave (#18, best untuned) is kept.

Pricing unknown ground (#18) was the first change of the step COST rather than of sources, and it gave the best untuned score (27.7, holdout 29.0); the body (radius 0.45) also pays for walls it walks beside, scraping, sliding and clipping corners, which the wave ignores (the tuner drove the diagonal discount of #4 down to 0.75, a hint that cutting corners near walls costs). Adding a CLEARANCE cost (each step discounted by the number of solid cells around it) makes plans keep to open floor and the middles of corridors, so walks get faster and fewer end in a slide or a press.

The map forgets free ground after roughly a thousand ticks, but eaten food regrows only after ~1200, so ground the agent harvested reappears as frontier while it is still bare and pulls the agent back for nothing. A slow SEEN memory (once known free, fading over a couple of thousand ticks) lowers what a frontier mark is worth on ground that was seen before, so exploration prefers virgin ground, where food has never been eaten, and returns to old ground only when the memory has faded, roughly when its food has regrown.

Every wave so far multiplies by a discount, so a target's pull decays exponentially with path length and only the ratio of two sources' strengths matters: a crumb of frontier two steps away routinely beats a sure meal fifteen steps away. An ADDITIVE wave (each step subtracts a walking cost, larger on unknown ground, floored at zero) makes pull fall off linearly, so strong sources (seen food, smell) keep their lead over long distances while faint frontier marks only matter nearby: a different far-versus-near trade-off, not a new source.

Pricing unknown ground helped (#18), but every unknown cell is priced alike, although walls are straight: an unknown cell that continues a seen wall line (walls on two opposite sides, or two wall cells in a row pointing at it) is very likely wall. MAP COMPLETION guesses those cells, so frontier marks on them stop calling (a false frontier along every wall the agent walks beside) and the wave passes them at half strength, so plans stop aiming at the hidden continuation of walls and head for real gaps.

The smell is painted at a waypoint straight out along the walkable bearing, so whenever the route bends the waypoint lands inside rock, and the wave then leads the agent into that wall to press (world 16: 106 idle presses, world 2: 100). Moving a smell painted on a solid cell to its open (and not guessed-wall) neighbours puts the target beside the wall on the walkable side, so the nose leads along walls toward the gap instead of into them; map completion and knowledge pricing (#23, best) are kept.

On the trap worlds the agent paces one small area for thousands of ticks because nothing there ever becomes less attractive for longer than the footprint trail lasts (a few thoughts). A slow HABITUATION field piles up wherever the agent dwells and fades over hundreds of ticks, and walking across over-familiar ground costs extra in the wave (a step cost, the kind of change that has paid: #18, #23), so plans out of a paced area get relatively cheaper than plans that cross it again, while ordinary foraging, which keeps moving, is barely touched.

The `bright` sense has never been used: ground is dark (~0.21), foliage, which is walkable but opaque and is where plants bear (and hide) food, is ~0.58, below the 0.6 that makes a morsel. Reading bright, walkable, non-morsel cells as LEAVES and giving them a weak source (silenced on the fresh trail so a clump once searched does not hold the agent) sends it into clumps where food hides behind leaves and regrows, on top of the best structure (#23: map completion + knowledge pricing).

Map completion (#23, best train 29.6) guesses only the one unknown cell that continues a wall line, so a wall seen for ten cells is predicted for one more and the plan still runs into its hidden continuation, and corners and rock bodies are not predicted at all. Making completion RECURSIVE (guesses count as wall for the next guess, so a line extends several cells with fading confidence) and filling unknown cells hemmed in by wall on four or more of eight sides predicts the hidden geometry further, so fewer false frontiers call and fewer plans aim through rock.

Wiping the plan every thought collapsed foraging (#16: 12.8), but that change also cut the wave's range to five cells, so it never tested the real question: how fast should the plan follow the world? EXPRESS LANES let the wave also jump two cells straight per pass, gated by the cell it jumps over (its leak, guessed wall and knowledge price), so the steady state is the same plan but news (a morsel seen, a meal gone, a door opened) crosses the map twice as fast; if the stale plateau is useful commitment, this will cost meals, if it is lag, it will pay.

Two changes of step price by knowledge (#18 unknown ground, #23 guessed walls) gave the only clear gains, while the helpers stacked around them (darkness weighting, footprint trail, frontier split, inline channels) may now be redundant or fitted to the training worlds. A MINIMAL law keeps only the knowledge-priced wave with map completion and source confinement, in ONE rule writing `value` directly: if it eats about as much, the night's structure is the knowledge pricing and a simpler law should generalise better to unseen worlds; if it drops, the helpers are load-bearing.

The minimal law fell to 24.6 (#29), so darkness and trail are load-bearing, and the best structure is the knowledge-priced wave with its helpers. The one remaining unpriced thing in it is a SEEN wall: every wall cell passes the wave by its own taught leak, alike for rock and door; door contrast (#19) gave the best holdout (31.2) on the older base. Here walls are priced by their door contrast inside #23 (map completion + unknown-ground price), and darkness no longer counts guessed-wall cells as unexplored, so the whole map is priced by what the agent knows: seen floor cheap, unknown dearer, guessed wall dearer still, rock nearly shut, doors open.

Every law of the night injects a seen morsel at full strength (thing * (1 - bad)) whatever the taught appetite says, so a nightcap the brain has learned to refuse still calls the agent across the map until it arrives, refuses and marks it bad; the harness's own source already carries that appetite. Scaling the morsel term by the source painted on it (appetite-weighted, hushed near bad things) makes the agent ignore things it does not want and saves those wasted trips; a poison-handling axis the night has not touched, on the new best base (#30).

Map completion so far predicts only WALLS; the price of unknown ground (#18) is then paid alike by a cell that obviously continues an open corridor or room and by one in the middle of nowhere. The other half of completion guesses an unknown cell that continues a line of open floor (open on two opposite sides, or two free cells in a row pointing at it) as probably floor and waives its unknown price, so plans run cheaply along the obvious continuation of corridors and rooms and the price still bites where the map gives no hint.

Predicted floor (#32: 30.5 untuned, holdout 30.5, the best honest number of the night) is used only to price steps; it also says which FRONTIER is worth walking to. A frontier mark on or beside a cell that continues open floor is the mouth of a corridor or room that goes on, while one that does not is more likely a nook against unseen rock, so frontier worth is multiplied by the predicted floor at and around it, next to the existing darkness weighting and the guessed-wall veto.

Raising a frontier's worth by predicted floor collapsed (#33: 22.1) while PRICING by predicted floor paid (#32: 30.5, holdout 30.5): knowledge belongs in step costs, not in what a source is worth. One price is still wrong: ground seen free a few hundred ticks ago fades back towards "unknown" and is charged as if it might be rock, although floors never move. A slow SEEN memory of floor (cleared by solid) waives the unknown price on remembered floor, so plans back across ground the agent has already walked cost what they really cost, while frontier and darkness still follow the fading map.

The footprint trail is load-bearing (#29 without it fell to 24.6) but acts only on the read-out, at the agent's own neighbours, so a plan can still lead the agent back along the corridor it just came by and only the first step is discouraged. Charging an extra step price for crossing fresh footprints moves the same idea into the plan (the kind of change that has paid all night): routes that re-walk the last few cells cost more along their whole length, so the agent loops round instead of shuttling, and old ground stays cheap once the footprints fade.
